newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam denies reported crackdown on Buddhists.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam denies reported crackdown on Buddhists.

text.p: Vietnam on Tuesday dismissed reports that security forces had arrested several prominent Buddhist monks and destroyed a Zen meditation centre in a sweep against religious dissidents.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman denied a report by the Paris-based International Buddhist Information Bureau that 200 police had surrounded Linh Mu pagoda on the banks of the Perfume River in the central city of Hue and arrested two monks.
He said the monks, Le Phu Thinh and Nguyen Chon Tam, had been invited to return to residences at which they were ordered to stay after their release from prison last year.

"According to the decision to release them from prison they had to return to residences outside Hue and Quang Tri, but the two men did not follow the decision... The local authorities had to invite them back to the previous residences."
A provincial official told Reuters that a car was sent on November 22 to pick the two men up and that their departure from the pagoda passed off peacably.
"This is an administrative matter, it's not a political or religious issue," he said. "We invited them politely to move to the other place..."

The Buddhist watchdog group said the "raid" was part of a government plan to take control of the 395-year-old pagoda, one of the treasured monuments of Vietnamese Buddhism and also one of the most active centres of Buddhist dissent.
Both Thinh and Tam were arrested and jailed in 1993 for taking part in a demonstration of 40,000 Buddhists for religious freedom in Hue.

Both monks belong to the now-banned Unified Buddhist Church of Vietnam (UBCV), the Buddhist church organisation in former South Vietnam until the victory of Hanoi's communist forces over the South in 1975.

The UBCV is still regarded by Buddhists in the south and abroad as the sole legitimate church organisation. However, the government regards the state-sponsored Vietnam Buddhist Church (VBC) as the only legal organisation for Buddhists in Vietnam.

The Foreign Ministry also dismissed a report by the International Buddhist Information Bureau that a pagoda in the central town of Dalat was destroyed and a superior monk, Truong Thanh Tam, arrested on October 30.
"In fact there is no such thing as the Long Tho pagoda Zen meditation centre," the spokesman said.

"Truong Thanh Tam took advantage of religious freedom to pretend to be a monk, occupy public land and compose a so-called prayer book to delude and dupe people, including the sexual abuse of women," he said.
He said local authorities had arrested Tam on charges of pursuing superstitious practices likely to cause harm and had retaken land his group had occupied.
A local VBC official said security forces had destroyed all but one building at the centre and arrested Tam and three nuns.
